title: The Hare and the Hound

full_text:
A swift hound, prized for his pedigree and keen hunting instincts, started a hare from a dense clover patch. Barking excitedly, the hound gave fierce chase across the rolling meadow, bounding over ditches and through bramble hedges. The hare, knowing every covert and twist of the land, darted with lightning speed, doubling back, leaping sideways, and sprinting for her very survival.

After a long, grueling chase, the panting hound began to tire, his tongue lolling from his jaws and his pace slackening until the nimble hare slipped beneath an impenetrable briar tangle and vanished from sight.

A goat herd who had watched the pursuit from a rocky knoll laughed loudly and called out: "Shame on you, noble hunter! A tiny, timid creature has outrun a great champion like you!"

The hound caught his breath, looked up at the herdsman, and replied with weary dignity: "You do not understand the difference between us, sir. I was running merely for my dinner; she was running for her life!"
moral: One runs for dinner, while the other runs for life itself.
